source_snapshot.criteria: System operates normally; BMC may show link disable/degrade for advanced RAS or correctable error for standard; front-panel light differs by RAS SKU; UEFI SEL may record the event.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes the operator boundary but its Linux SSH grep conflicts with the Windows procedure, does not prove the selected link or physical indicator, and weakens host trust.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires FAE-controlled topology-aware injection and SKU-specific evidence instead of generic log matching.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Adjacent CRC-infinite and link-layer cases cannot replace data-lane failover behavior or its standard-versus-advanced RAS branches.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The approved safety and verdict rules reserve disruptive injection, recovery and DUT outcome to qualified humans and require complete raw evidence.

original_test_intent: Inject a UPI data-lane failover condition into each approved socket/link target and demonstrate that the platform remains operational while logging and front-panel behavior match the CPU's standard or advanced RAS capability.
original_method: An FAE/operator on an isolated Windows SUT enables the exact listed EDKII settings, verifies ITP topology and port mapping against the physical UPI link, performs one approved `injUpiDataLinkFailover` action, resumes the system, assesses live link/system health, collects Windows RAS, BMC and post-recovery UEFI evidence plus the front-panel state, then restores all debug settings. Evidence and expected branch must be fixed before execution.
manual_activity: The FAE/operator must identify the actual UPI socket/port rather than a similarly numbered PCIe slot, enable and restore BIOS controls, run one bounded injector action, observe the SKU-dependent lamp, and recover any degraded link or crashed system.
required_inputs: Board/CPU topology, UPI link/socket/port map and CPU standard-versus-advanced RAS SKU
Supported Intel ITP/CScripts build with checksum and exact injUpiDataLinkFailover parameter semantics
Expected link state and exact OS/BMC/UEFI records for each supported SKU
Front-panel indicator map, injection timeout/abort and vendor recovery/restoration plan
safety_requirements: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, independent console and explicit owner/FAE approval
Preserve pre-state logs and topology rather than clearing evidence
Cross-check Cscript port identity against physical UPI topology before injection
Stop for wrong target, uncontrolled degradation, thermal/power fault, lost console, crash or no-boot
Never auto-repeat; restore debug settings and link health only through the approved recovery
agent_execution_scope: Validate supplied package identity, target map and non-mutating baseline artifacts
Collect authorized complete post-event OS/BMC/UEFI evidence and correlate timestamps
Do not choose the port, enter BIOS, invoke Cscripts, inject a lane failure, reset/retrain/power-cycle the system or assign the final verdict
engineer_actions: Approve topology and standard/advanced SKU classification
Define exact one-shot injection parameters, expected degradation/failover and recovery
Replace dmesg with the authoritative Windows RAS source or change the OS requirement
Convert every optional `may` into deterministic per-SKU acceptance and define indicator/SEL behavior

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The proposed SSH dmesg/SEL tail is only partial evidence, runs against an unspecified host OS despite Windows in the procedure, discards context, cannot establish link failover or the lamp state, and uses unsafe SSH settings.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: The injection remains an exact FAE-operated Intel Cscript action; agent commands, if approved, are read-only evidence exports from the actual Windows and BMC interfaces.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: `ei.injUpiDataLinkFailover(socket,port,1,0x3)`, topology queries, Socket 0~N and 30/10-minute estimates are preserved without guessing target or parameter meaning.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the manifest target to recorded ITP topology, capture synchronized pre/post link counters and Windows WHEA plus BMC/UEFI exports, execute one FAE-approved injection, document SKU-specific front-panel behavior, verify bounded recovery and compare BIOS settings.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds deterministic SKU branches, correct Windows evidence, link-health proof, explicit aborts and restoration without changing the failover stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic log grep cannot show which lane/link failed over, whether operation was maintained or whether the correct SKU-specific physical response occurred.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong port selection or unexpected lane degradation can isolate CPU traffic, destabilize the SUT or produce persistent RAS state.

project_override_considerations: Inputs and human approval make this conditionally executable, but critical fault injection, BIOS changes and physical observation remain outside autonomous agent authority. A missing package or operator is a blocked run, not a hardware failure.
expected_evidence: FAE approval, exact SUT/CPU/RAS-SKU/firmware/OS identity and physical UPI topology
Package hash, topology/port-map output, selected link rationale and full injection transcript
Pre/post BIOS setting and link-health comparison
Complete Windows RAS, BMC SEL and recovered UEFI SEL with synchronized timestamps
SKU-specific front-panel photo/video and normal-operation checks
Recovery/restoration record and engineer PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED disposition

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The SUT is booted into Windows while dmesg is requested, and `may record` leaves BMC/UEFI results non-deterministic. The source also needs an authoritative mapping from standard/advanced CPU RAS SKU to required logs and lamp behavior.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A concrete Intel injection call and intended SKU branches exist, so the case is not intrinsically undefined. It becomes executable only when the package, exact target, deterministic oracle, recovery and qualified operator are supplied; failed readiness is reported as BLOCKED rather than DUT FAIL.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 7 Wistron-System RAS-00727-V003: approve the board/CPU UPI topology, socket/port target and Intel ITP/CScripts version/hash plus `injUpiDataLinkFailover(...,1,0x3)` semantics; define bounded abort/recovery and BIOS restoration; reconcile the Windows boot with dmesg; and replace BMC/UEFI `may` language with deterministic standard-versus-advanced RAS SKU log, link-health, normal-operation and front-panel acceptance.

review_improvement: This review makes target identity and the two CPU-SKU outcome branches testable while preventing a generic PCIe/UPI grep from standing in for actual data-lane failover coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: UPI data-lane failover is a topology-sensitive link event: an integer port in an Intel debug shell is not trustworthy until correlated to the physical socket-to-socket path. The expected response also changes with CPU RAS capability, so `may` cannot serve as a pass rule without a known SKU matrix. Normal operation should include link state and workload/health continuity, not merely a booted console. Because Windows is mandated, the OS oracle must be WHEA/ETW or another approved Windows record instead of assumed dmesg. These issues require engineering inputs and human-controlled injection, but the underlying method is sufficiently defined for REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION.
